articles.title: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping Costume Designer Reveals Inspiration Process
articles.summary: A prequel to The Hunger Games, The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping is set 24 years before the events of The Hunger Games and 40 years after The Ballad of Songbirds Snakes.
articles.content: The red carpet has been abuzz with Elle Fanning's outrageous fashion choices as Effie Trinket in recent weeks, leaving fans and critics alike to wonder what inspired such daring style decisions. Fanning's character is a nod to the young Effie Trinket from The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, a theatrical production set to premiere on November 20. This new take on the classic tale is based on Suzanne Collins' novel of the same name, published in 2025. It serves as a prequel to the original series, taking place 24 years before the events of The Hunger Games and 40 years after The Ballad of Songbirds Snakes. Bina Daigeler, the costume designer behind this new film, has been instrumental in bringing Effie's eccentric style to life. Working closely with her team, she created every single outfit from scratch, drawing on vintage specialists for a few select accessories. This meticulous approach allowed Daigeler to infuse each look with its own unique personality. To ensure that the costumes accurately reflected the distinctiveness of each district, Daigeler began by curating a mood board that highlighted the aesthetic differences between these 13 regions. To create costumes that would accurately reflect the distinctiveness of each district in The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, Daigeler drew inspiration from a range of designers, including Alexander McQueen and John Galliano. "It was really like old couture fashion," she recalls, referencing the timeless appeal of these iconic houses. Daigeler's goal was to create pieces that would remain relevant for years to come, as she believes this is crucial when working on such an esteemed franchise. This approach ensured that her designs would be a fitting tribute to the series. Daigeler worked closely with Drusilla Sickle, played by Glenn Close, who sought to find a common thread throughout her costumes. To achieve this, Daigeler incorporated "cool accessories" to give Sickle's character strength and depth, culminating in one striking finale look that would leave a lasting impression. Daigeler aimed to capture Effie Trinket's personality through her fashion choices, resulting in a distinct concept for each outfit. Effie Trinket herself was a central focus of Daigeler's efforts, given her background as a stylist and her love of fashion. The film explores how young Effie Trinket evolved into the stylish character portrayed by Elizabeth Banks, with early scenes showcasing her more improvisational approach to fashion. As Effie's character progresses, her outfits become increasingly polished, reflecting her growing status as a fashion icon in the Capitol. Effie Trinket's outfits are not just about aesthetics; they're also about conveying her character's emotional state and social standing. In the Reaping scene of The Hunger Games: Sunrise, Effie's fashion choices reflect a growing sense of confidence and poise. Daigeler, the costume designer, sourced vintage pieces from around the world to create Effie's distinctive style. One notable example is her butterfly crystal rings, which add a touch of whimsy to her overall look. These subtle details are just a few of the fashion Easter eggs hidden throughout the film. Haymitch Abernathy also undergoes a sartorial transformation in The Hunger Games: Sunrise. His costume designer aimed for a more understated yet still stylish approach. Daigeler notes that Haymitch's clothes were deliberately aged to give them a worn, lived-in look. Effie Trinket's attention to detail extended to the character of President Snow as well, with a focus on conveying power through his attire. The designer worked closely with a London tailor who had previously collaborated with her, incorporating World War II military-inspired cuts and heavy fabrics into Snow's suits, which were then elevated with hand-embroidered lapels. The outfits were designed to reflect the character's authoritative presence, while also incorporating subtle fantasy elements to add depth and visual interest. articles.title: Hailey Bieber's Viral Blue Sheet Mask Features Pyderin's Hydrovuster Line
articles.summary: The mask is part of a comprehensive skincare routine that has sent shockwaves through the beauty community, with Hailey Bieber showcasing an array of products on her Instagram post.
articles.content: Hailey Bieber's Instagram post has sent shockwaves through the beauty community, showcasing a comprehensive skincare routine featuring an array of products to soothe and hydrate her skin. Among the diverse collection of traditional sheet masks, LED devices, rubber masks, and rich creams is one product that has particularly caught attention - a blue-tinted sheet mask that has sparked widespread curiosity. The mask in question is part of Pyderin's Hydrovuster line, specifically designed to provide hydration and calmness to sensitive skin. According to Jennifer Seo, head concierge at Aneue, the brand behind this innovative product, the Hydrovuster collection was created with soothing post-treatment skin or reactive skin in mind. The blue coloration of the mask is not merely for aesthetic appeal; it's a result of the inclusion of blue azulene, an anti-inflammatory ingredient that also reduces redness. The unique combination of ingredients in Hailey Bieber's viral blue K-beauty sheet mask is what sets it apart from other similar products on the market. According to Dr. Chang Son, a board-certified dermatologist based in NYC, this mask provides an intense dose of hydration that can be particularly beneficial for dry or dehydrated skin. The serum used in the mask is pharmaceutical-grade and contains PDRN in its highest purity. Seo explains that the treatment's high concentration allows it to synergize effectively with other key ingredients like blue azulene and mucin, promoting healing and soothing of the skin. Notably, the mask uses domestically sourced PDRN extracted from Korean salmon, which is a distinct advantage over some competing brands that may use internationally sourced PDRN derived from different types of fish. This difference in sourcing could potentially affect the purity and effectiveness of the product. Dr. Son highlights another key benefit of the sodium PDRN used in this mask: its enhanced water solubility makes it more suitable for topical applications and easier to incorporate into skin care products, such as creams or sheet masks like Hailey Bieber's viral sensation. This improved bioavailability could contribute to a more efficient delivery of the active ingredients to the skin, further amplifying their benefits. Pyderin's sheet mask contains 99 percent pure PDRN, which is also small enough at 97 kilodaltons to penetrate deep into the skin. This high concentration and optimal size of PDRN enable it to effectively deliver its benefits. The combination of pure PDRN and blue azulene makes Pyderin suitable for regular use on all skin types and tones, especially after treatments that can leave skin sensitive or irritated. Son notes that this mask would be particularly beneficial for patients with chronic dry or inflamed skin like rosacea. The mask is currently out of stock, but it will soon become available via Amazon in mid-to-late November. articles.title: Nvidia Cofounder Jensen Huang Resigns Amid Allegations of Personal Scandal
articles.summary: Jensen Huang has resigned as Nvidia CEO amidst allegations of a personal scandal involving a woman linked to China, sparking concerns about potential conflicts of interest and export regulations violations.
articles.content: Nvidia's cofounder Jensen Huang has resigned as CEO amidst allegations of a personal scandal. His resignation on November 12 came after it was discovered he had been involved in an affair with a woman linked to China, sparking concerns about potential conflicts of interest and export regulations violations. The controversy centres around Nvidia's business dealings with her company in Singapore, which received billions of dollars' worth of sales under Huang's leadership. It has also raised questions about whether his personal relationships influenced major business decisions. Huang's swift return to X after resigning was a surprise move that left many wondering how he managed to mobilize so quickly. Using cutting-edge technology such as Rubin GPUs, Huang may have accelerated the process of reviewing his own actions, potentially reducing what would normally take months into just a few days. However, this rapid turnaround didn't sit well with Nvidia's board, which swiftly rejected his offer to return. In fact, the board's decision was made so quickly that it seemed almost instantaneous, like a data center in Texas consuming massive amounts of water in a short amount of time. The search for Huang's replacement is now underway, but the push to restore him to his former position has not dissipated. A petition calling on Nvidia to rehire Huang has garnered over 200,000 signatures, with even the President of the United States weighing in on the matter by expressing support for Huang's return. Despite the board's rejection and a company-wide message from Kress assuring employees that "we got this," the efforts to bring Huang back are still ongoing. Some reports suggest that Huang may have had personal discussions with at least one board member about his potential reinstatement, leaving some directors open to the possibility. The Jensen affair continues to cast a long shadow over Nvidia's biggest IPO in history, dominating discussions at the New York Times DealBook conference just one day after the company's earnings call. Despite Anthropic's preparations for its historic market debut, the focus remained on Huang and his tumultuous tenure as CEO. OpenAI's Sam Altman and Greg Brockman took to the stage, expressing admiration for Huang but stopping short of endorsing his reinstatement. In a striking display of loyalty, Anduril CEO Palmer Luckey defended Jensen, arguing that no one could replace him in this critical moment due to his personal relationships with key business partners. According to Luckey, these connections are what make people willing to do business with Nvidia. Elon Musk's outrage over Huang's ousting was palpable as he likened the situation to the Chicago Bulls firing Michael Jordan during a playoff hot streak. In informal conversations during breaks at the conference, it became clear that opinions on the matter are sharply divided. The fervor surrounding Huang's reinstatement at Nvidia is a stark reminder of how corporate interests often take precedence over ethics and national security concerns. Those advocating for his return point to his exceptional leadership skills, arguing that he is irreplaceable and that letting him go would be a disservice to the company's past achievements. However, this line of thinking ignores the fact that Huang's personal behavior has raised serious questions about his fitness as a CEO, including allegations of dishonesty with the board and potential violations of export regulations. The cult-like reverence for founders who have built successful companies into global brands is also on full display in this debate, implying that their unique abilities should be left unchecked. Huang's decision to hand over senior executive posts to family members who showed interest in the chip business later in life has raised questions about nepotism and its impact on shareholders. While it may seem like a way to share power within the company, the practice of giving key positions to relatives can actually cost investors dearly, particularly if these individuals are not well-equipped for their roles. Moreover, Huang's failure to prepare a succession plan for Nvidia has left the company vulnerable in case he is no longer able to lead it. This oversight has been criticized by other business leaders, including Satya Nadella, who pointed out that companies need to have a clear plan in place for leadership transitions. Huang would be wise to abandon his efforts to regain control at Nvidia and instead focus on repairing his personal relationships. His family dynamics are in need of attention, as is his reputation, which could benefit from his cooperation with lawyers to address any outstanding issues. This approach would also enable him to avoid being associated with the company if its fortunes were to decline, allowing him to maintain a positive public image. articles.title: US Data Centers Drive Economic Growth but Create Labor Shortage
articles.summary: The rapid expansion of data centers in the US is driving significant economic growth, but it has created a pressing challenge for the telecommunications industry due to a shortage of skilled workers.
articles.content: The rapid expansion of data centers is driving significant economic growth in the US, with an estimated $800 billion expected to be spent on these facilities by 2026 alone. However, this boom has created a pressing challenge for the telecommunications industry: it requires a workforce that can build and connect these data centers, but there simply aren't enough workers available to meet demand. According to AT&T CEO John Stankey, the shortage of skilled construction and technician workers is becoming increasingly urgent. By 2032, he estimates that nearly 200,000 additional workers will be needed to keep pace with industry growth. Stankey warns that unless this issue is addressed, the US risks being unable to support the rapid development of AI infrastructure. He notes that all these new data centers need to be connected if we want to continue growing as an economy. As a result, Stankey sees an opportunity for Gen Z to enter the workforce and fill this critical gap, particularly since the traditional college-to-career pipeline is becoming less reliable. As workers in various industries struggle to find qualified candidates, a significant gap has emerged in the job market for technical roles such as fiber splicers and telecommunications installers. These entry-level positions often don't require a bachelor's degree, but instead offer on-the-job training that equips workers with the necessary skills. According to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, the median annual salary for these jobs is around $70,000, although total compensation can reach six figures when overtime and bonuses are factored in. Companies like AT&T are actively hiring for these roles, with a spokesperson explaining that they prioritize candidates' skills and potential over their educational background. This approach has proven effective, as evidenced by the success of new hires who receive extensive training before being certified to perform complex tasks. The demand for skilled tradespeople extends beyond telecommunications, with the data center construction boom putting pressure on the supply of electricians, plumbers, and HVAC technicians. The Alliance for America's Skilled Trades, a coalition of leading companies including AT&T, Meta, Google, and Ford, has been working to address the severe shortage of skilled tradespeople in the US labor market. According to Stankey, CEO of AT&T, the existing stigma surrounding careers that don't require a college degree is a major obstacle to filling the estimated 1.7 million skilled trades openings every year through 2035. Stankey emphasizes that careers like telecommunications and fiber installation are not only stable but also lucrative, with salaries reaching up to $70,000 per year, without the need for a four-year degree. He argues that these jobs offer a unique combination of physical and mental challenges, which should be valued equally alongside traditional white-collar professions. The solution to this labor shortage lies in changing societal attitudes towards work, Stankey suggests, by recognizing the validity and worth of careers that don't conform to traditional expectations. articles.title: Plestia Alaqad Publishes Diary-Memoir The Eyes of Gaza
articles.summary: The book chronicles Plestia Alaqad's experiences as a young Palestinian journalist during the weeks following October 7 in Gaza.
articles.content: Plestia Alaqad's decision to publish her diary-memoir, The Eyes of Gaza, has brought a deeply personal account of life in Gaza to the world stage. As she reflects on this choice, Alaqad acknowledges that making her intimate and private writings public was a challenging task. The book chronicles Alaqad's experiences as a young Palestinian journalist during the harrowing weeks following October 7 in Gaza. Her own journey began when she returned home in 2022 after studying new media and journalism at Eastern Mediterranean University in Cyprus. Alaqad's reporting often focused on ordinary people, positioning herself as their voice in the midst of chaos. In the early days, she spoke with her neighbors and local children, capturing moments of tenderness amidst the turmoil. Her own account also includes the expulsion of over 100,000 Gazans in the first few days. Her stories were largely shared through her Instagram account, which gained a significant following of around two million people. Many of her images were republished by prominent media outlets like the BBC, The New York Times, PBS NewsHour, and The Washington Post. Plestia Alaqad's reporting style is characterized by its relatability, capturing the mundane in extraordinary situations. She has relocated to Lebanon, where she is pursuing her master’s degree, a significant departure from her Gaza roots. The sense of community in Gaza is one aspect that Alaqad cherishes deeply. She recalls the close-knit relationships within her building with fondness. Her neighbors were like family to her; they offered support and companionship whenever needed, exemplified by Dana, who lived next door and was a constant presence in her life. Plestia Alaqad's writing ambitions extend far beyond her current projects. She believes it's essential for people like herself to continue creating work that showcases their talents and artistic expression. Her statement "There's more to us than being occupied" reflects the sentiment of many individuals who feel suffocated by the pressures of daily life, leaving little time for personal pursuits. Alaqad's desire is to produce content that highlights human stories and experiences, allowing readers to connect with others on a deeper level. In recent times, Alaqad has been involved in writing about people she finds inspiring, such as Renad Atallah, whose story was featured in The New Arab. Additionally, Alaqad has started her own newsletter on Substack, where she shares personal essays every week, often focusing on themes like Gaza, girlhood, and friendship. Alaqad's ultimate goal is to tell stories about a free Palestine one day, and as a journalist, she feels that her work remains incomplete without continuing to report from the ground in Gaza, sharing Palestinian stories with the world. As a voracious reader of nonfiction books and memoirs, Alaqad has always been fascinated by people's experiences and stories. Her curiosity about human nature is matched only by her desire to learn from others' perspectives. Alaqad's affinity for personal writings extends beyond literary works, with Franz Kafka's letters and the correspondence between Ghassan Kanafani and Ghada al-Samman being particular favorites. This interest in understanding people's thoughts and emotions has led her to appreciate personal reflections and diaries. Growing up, Alaqad kept a diary as a way of expressing herself without fear of judgment. For her, journaling was, and remains, a safe space where she can write freely. It is this need for self-expression that drives her creative endeavors. The first product under Alaqad's brand Neya will be a journal, designed to provide a personal and secure outlet for users. Available in four colors, each journal features gentle reminders on the hardcover and inspirational quotes throughout its pages. As a refugee who has experienced the trauma of displacement, journaling serves as a vital lifeline for reconnecting with oneself amidst chaos. The transition from private diarist to public figure was daunting, particularly when one's personal thoughts and emotions are shared with a global audience. Sharing intimate moments with strangers can be overwhelming, especially when those moments involve pain, loss, and resilience in the face of unimaginable circumstances. Living between two worlds - the comfort and security of education and opportunities abroad versus the harsh realities of war-torn homelands - presents its own set of challenges. Time seems to have stood still in Gaza as the world around it continues to evolve and progress at an unprecedented pace. The stark contrast between stagnation and growth is a defining characteristic of life in this war-torn region, where one can find despair alongside resilience on every corner. The photo series "Eyes of Gaza" poignantly captures these disparate elements, juxtaposing sorrow with optimism in striking visuals that leave viewers spellbound. By confronting the complexities of human emotions, the photographer aims to inspire action and empathy among those who experience the images. articles.title: Meta Unveils Third-Generation Ray-Ban Glasses at Meta Connect Event
articles.summary: The new Meta Ray-Ban glasses have undergone some cosmetic updates and performance enhancements but lack significant advancements compared to predecessors.
articles.content: The latest iteration of Meta's Ray-Ban glasses has been met with a lukewarm response following the company's Meta Connect event. The third-generation model was unveiled alongside several other products, including audio-only glasses and an updated lineup of VR headsets. The new Meta Ray-Ban glasses have undergone some cosmetic updates and performance enhancements, but they don't stray far from their predecessors in terms of innovation. This lack of significant advancements is particularly notable when compared to other recent models released by the company. Despite this, there's still much to appreciate about these premium smart glasses. One of the most striking aspects of the new Meta Ray-Ban glasses is their sleek design. Available in three frame styles, Wayfarer, Zena, and Aviator, each style offers a unique take on classic Ray-Ban designs. The frames are also available in various colors, many of which feature semi-transparent materials that allow users to glimpse the internal components. The Gen 3 Meta Ray-Ban glasses carry a hefty price tag of $449, raising questions about their value proposition given the relatively minor upgrades they offer. With numerous variations of Meta-branded smart glasses now on the market, it's unclear whether these latest models should be considered the default choice for those in the market for new glasses. The limited availability of the Gen 3 Meta Ray-Ban glasses is another point worth considering. For now, only three frame styles are available, and each style can be paired with a range of colors to suit individual tastes. The Ray-Ban Meta (Gen 3) frames I wore for this review were Aviators in Havana, a brown tortoiseshell color that was a welcome change from the usual dark and boxy options. Unfortunately, it's clear that these new frame shapes aren't without their drawbacks, particularly when it comes to fit. While some may appreciate the bold look of the Zena or Aviator frames, I found them to be excessively oversized - 10mm wider than even the smallest Wayfarer frames. This made them feel awkward on my face and difficult to wear with confidence. Clear lenses didn't help, as they only added to the bulkiness. The fit issues were exacerbated by the fact that these frames need to be adjusted professionally, either at a Meta store or an optician's office. While this may not be a problem for those who purchase in person, it can be inconvenient for online shoppers looking for a hassle-free experience. And let's be clear - $529 is no small investment. The bulkiness of the frames also caused some issues with the glasses' fit on my nose. They constantly slipped down to the point where I considered purchasing after-market silicon tips to keep them in place. This was frustrating, especially given the premium price tag. The Meta Glasses' default clear transition lenses may offer flexibility for wearers, but they don't necessarily suit every frame style. In this case, the Aviator shape felt more suited to sunglasses than everyday wear, which made me wonder if these frames are worth the hefty price tag. The action button has become a staple feature in recent Meta glasses models, and it's now available on the Gen 3 as well. This customizable shortcut allows users to trigger specific actions without having to use voice commands - for instance, I set mine to read my latest text message. Battery life is another area where Gen 3 has seen some improvement over its predecessor. According to Meta, these frames can last up to nine hours on a single charge and the accompanying charging case adds an additional fifty hours of juice. However, it's worth noting that battery performance can fluctuate significantly depending on usage patterns. Continuous audio playback is a good indicator of how well a device manages its power consumption - in my experience with Gen 3, I managed to squeeze about six hours of continuous audio playback from my pair. Features like Live AI, which utilizes the camera to analyze surroundings, tend to drain batteries more quickly than others. An extra microphone has been added to Gen 3, and Meta claims that this will enhance sound quality for phone and video calls made with these glasses. During my testing, I didn't experience any complaints regarding audio quality on my previous model - but those who spoke to me over the phone while wearing Gen 3 reported that I sounded clearer than usual. A comparison with other wireless earbuds is also worth considering - I took a few phone calls using my AirPods Pro 2 and found that Gen 3 performed similarly, if not slightly better. However, it's essential to keep in mind that the sound quality may vary depending on individual preferences. The new Ray-Ban Meta glasses come equipped with all the same advanced AI features as Meta's other products. Powered by Muse Spark, these AI capabilities have resulted in more natural-sounding conversations and fewer errors. However, some users may miss the distinctive celebrity voices that were previously available. Meta's emphasis on its smart glasses is set to increase as its AI agent, Muse, continues to evolve. The company showcased Muse on its glasses during a recent conference, although this feature has yet to be officially rolled out to the public. Once available, users will be able to interact with their personal assistant through their glasses and share live video feed from the device's cameras. The integration of AI features like Muse into Meta's smart glasses may also pave the way for more aggressive marketing of Meta One subscription plans. The company has already demonstrated a willingness to charge extra for certain features, such as its new hearing enhancement tool. Additionally, some users are still waiting for another hearing-related feature, Conversation Focus, which was announced over a year ago. Meta's business strategy may lead to a shift in how users interact with their devices and the services they offer. The company is likely to push for more comprehensive adoption of its subscription plans, potentially making certain features exclusive to paying customers. This move could have significant implications for the future of wearable technology and user experience. The recent update to my Meta (Gen 3) glasses has brought about some changes that are worth noting. One of the first things I see when adjusting my settings is an invitation to sign up for Meta One in order to access additional photo storage capabilities. This promotion raises questions about the company's plans for subscription-based services and their potential impact on user experience. A notable improvement in the Gen 3 glasses is the option to opt out of data collection, specifically the ability to train AI models using visual data captured by the device. When I ask Meta AI a question, my glasses no longer store images or share them with contractors employed by the company. While this doesn't address all privacy concerns, it's an improvement that acknowledges some of the user's wishes. The recent shift in the market and technological advancements have made me reevaluate whether Gen 3 is worth the investment for most people. The non-Ray-Ban line from Meta offers similar features at a lower starting price point of $249. Considering this, the premium finish associated with the Ray-Ban branding on the Gen 3 model may not be enough to justify the higher cost. The current market also presents an alternative option in the form of last year's Gen 2 model, which still carries the Ray-Ban brand and offers a solid choice for those who value the premium finish. Furthermore, older frames from Gen 1 are available at $224, providing another viable option for consumers. The latest iteration of the Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses may still hold some appeal, but it's a subtle upgrade compared to its predecessors. For those who prioritize style above all else, the Gen 3 model offers an updated look that's sure to turn heads. Ultimately, with so many options on the market, it seems the only compelling reasons to choose the Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3 are personal taste or a desire for extended battery life, and even then, it may not be enough to sway most consumers. In the same period, his overall record stands at 320-271-16, resulting in substantial profits for those following his recommendations. Tierney's insights are not limited to specific teams or matchups but encompass broader trends and patterns within the league. articles.content: American Airlines has officially retired its Flagship First international service, marking the end of an era for the carrier. The decision to retire Flagship First comes after years of speculation about American's plans to revamp its long-haul seating options. The airline is replacing its international-style first-class product with larger and more modern business-class cabins on its marquee planes, featuring next-generation Flagship Suites. These upgraded business-class seats will boast features such as sliding privacy doors and superior technology, which many flyers are likely to welcome as a significant upgrade. However, there's also a sense of nostalgia surrounding the retirement of Flagship First, which was once touted as American's most exclusive cabin option. American's decision to retire its long-haul first-class product is in line with industry trends, where many carriers have opted to sunset their premium first-class offerings in favor of improved business-class seats. These upgraded cabins take up less space and are generally considered more profitable for airlines. American Airlines has been operating its iconic Flagship First class on certain routes for years, but that era is coming to an end. The airline will be retiring this exclusive long-haul seat in favor of more modern and efficient configurations. The decision marks a significant shift for American, which still offers the Polaris Business Class on some flights, as seen on United Airlines' aircraft. However, the Flagship First experience has been a unique offering that sets American apart from its competitors in terms of comfort and luxury. American is currently retrofitting its Boeing 777-300ER fleet to accommodate 70 new Flagship Suites in business-class, replacing the dedicated first-class cabin. This move will not only enhance passenger experience but also optimize seating capacity on these planes. American Airlines has announced that it will stop selling its Flagship First cabin on the A321T configuration after March 28. This decision is likely a result of the airline's transition to its new A321XLR planes, which are being introduced onto top cross-country flights. The retirement of Flagship First marks a positive change for passengers, as it allows them to choose from more lie-flat seats, regardless of whether they're paying cash or using miles. American Airlines' new business-class product is a significant improvement over its previous offering in the Flagship First cabin, with features like extra-spacious seats and bulkhead rows. The airline's decision to upgrade its business-class product also means that passengers will enjoy amenities previously reserved for first-class travelers. This includes perks like more legroom, wider seats, and other comfort-enhancing features. By eliminating the Flagship First option, American Airlines is giving passengers a better choice when it comes to upgrading their travel experience. As part of this transition, American Airlines is introducing its new A321XLR planes onto key routes, which will feature the upgraded business-class product. This move will not only enhance passenger comfort but also optimize seating capacity on these planes. The retirement of Flagship First marks a significant change for American Airlines' premium offerings. Passengers holding Flagship business-class tickets will now have access to exclusive lounges on qualifying routes. This benefit extends to those traveling in Flagship Business and Flagship Business Plus on international, transcontinental, and Hawaii flights. In addition to lounge access, these passengers can also enjoy meal service in the airline's restaurant-style dining rooms located in Dallas, Los Angeles, and Miami. However, this experience is only available on a space-available basis, indicating that availability may be limited. The removal of Flagship First as an official cabin may not have an immediate impact on seating capacity. Despite its demise, some loyal American Airlines customers are expressing mixed emotions about the retirement of Flagship First. For those who have had the opportunity to experience the cabin, it's a bittersweet ending. Some passengers have praised the unique touches that set Flagship First apart from other premium cabins. One industry expert who has flown in Flagship First on multiple occasions notes that while the service may not be drastically different from other business-class offerings, there are still some elevated amenities worth appreciating. The seats themselves will not disappear overnight as American Airlines continues to operate its Boeing 777-300ER fleet with a mix of old and new configurations. The retirement of American Airlines' most exclusive long-haul seat, Flagship First, will be a gradual process that stretches into 2027. Despite this, the airline is already planning to market the former first-class seats on its Boeing 777-300ER fleet as business-class in the future. While passengers who opt for these upgraded business-class seats won't receive full first-class service, they will still enjoy elevated seating. This marks a significant change from the previous configuration, where Flagship First offered unparalleled luxury and exclusivity. As American Airlines continues to modernize its fleet, the legacy of its most premium planes is being redefined, with some now offering more accessible yet still luxurious amenities. The shift reflects the evolving expectations of travelers seeking high-end experiences without the hefty price tag associated with traditional first-class service. articles.title: The Hunger Games Franchise Draws Inspiration from Ancient Greece and Rome
articles.summary: A resurgence in popularity for The Hunger Games has been fueled by recent book releases and an upcoming movie adaptation, which explores the world of Panem.
articles.content: The Hunger Games franchise is experiencing a resurgence in popularity, thanks to the release of two prequel books in recent years and an upcoming movie adaptation hitting theaters on November 20. Author Suzanne Collins' Classical inspirations are becoming increasingly evident as she expands our understanding of the world of Panem. Collins has shared her creative process with audiences multiple times, revealing that she was inspired by a peculiar combination of reality television and war footage while channel surfing one day. This unusual pairing sparked her imagination and led to the creation of The Hunger Games series. Her writing began as an exploration of just war theory, merging the concepts of reality TV and deadly combat. The origins of the Games themselves owe a debt to ancient Greek and Roman traditions. Collins drew inspiration from the myth of Theseus and the Minotaur, as well as the brutal gladiatorial combat that was a staple of Roman entertainment. By combining these elements, she crafted the core plot and style of The Hunger Games. Collins' use of Classical influences is not limited to her creative process but also permeates the world-building of Panem itself. Major Capitol residents are given names that echo ancient Greek and Roman figures, while the terminology used by the people of Panem bears a striking resemblance to historical accounts from these cultures. The connections between The Hunger Games and ancient death battles may be apparent even to non-experts in Classical history. However, upon closer examination, it becomes clear just how deeply embedded these influences are within the franchise. From names to terminology, Collins' use of Greek and Roman history serves as a commentary on the darker aspects of these cultures. This appropriation of historical elements highlights the dangers of authoritarian regimes co-opting cultural heritage for their own purposes. By examining The Hunger Games through this lens, readers can gain a deeper understanding of how power is exercised and maintained in societies that value control above all else. Collins' use of Classical influences extends beyond the names and terminology used within the series. Her depiction of the Capitol as a decadent and oppressive force also draws parallels with ancient Rome's own imperial excesses. This commentary on the dangers of unchecked power serves as a warning to readers about the consequences of allowing authority to go unchallenged. The influence of Greek and Roman history on The Hunger Games is not limited to Collins' creative process or world-building. Her use of Classical terminology and concepts has also been incorporated into the language used by characters within the series, further blurring the lines between fiction and reality. The Hunger Games series has been praised for its thought-provoking commentary on authoritarian regimes, but few fans realize just how deeply rooted in ancient Greek and Roman culture it is. From the names of Capitol residents to the terminology used by Panem's citizens, references to Classical history are scattered throughout the franchise. This blending of fiction and reality has sparked debate among scholars about the implications of such appropriations. One of the most striking examples of Roman influence on The Hunger Games setting is the country itself, which gets its name from the Latin word for bread. Collins has acknowledged that bread plays a significant role in the series, often symbolizing life and sustenance. The Capitol's use of food as a tool to control the population is another example of how ancient cultures are woven into the narrative. By keeping the districts hungry, the Capitol ensures they have no energy left to resist its rule, highlighting the darker aspects of Roman and Greek culture. This theme is perhaps most evident in Peeta Mellark's profession as a baker, where his gift of bread helped keep Katniss alive long enough to spark the rebellion. The significance of bread in both the arena and outside it underscores the Capitol's calculated use of food to maintain its grip on power. The concept of "bread and circuses has been explicitly referenced by Plutarch in Mockingjay, a phrase coined by Roman writer Juvenal in his work Satires. This idea highlights how authoritarian regimes often use entertainment as a distraction from their own brutality and oppression. This borrowing from ancient cultures is not limited to terminology alone; the series also draws on Classical concepts and ideas. The Capitol's manipulation of information and its use of propaganda are just two examples of how Roman and Greek history have been incorporated into the narrative. The Hunger Games franchise has been praised for its thought-provoking commentary, but it also raises important questions about cultural appropriation and the implications of drawing from ancient cultures in modern storytelling. The Capitol's excesses are a stark reminder of the Roman Empire's own decadence, as described by Juvenal in his scathing critiques of Rome's elite. The citizens' gluttony is so extreme that they intentionally induce vomiting to make room for more food. Their reliance on bread and circuses is a deliberate ploy to distract them from the darker aspects of their society, as Juvenal so astutely observed. The parallels between Panem and ancient Rome are striking, particularly in the Capitol's use of entertainment to manipulate its citizens. The annual spectacle of child deaths and Victor celebrations serves as a cruel reminder that even those who have no desire for violence can revel in the power to do so. This insidious dynamic is a hallmark of Juvenal's Rome, where bread and circuses are used to keep the population in a state of complacent apathy. However, this complacency is short-lived, as the Capitol has learned through experience. When the food and entertainment that have lulled its citizens into submission are suddenly taken away, they can quickly turn on their oppressors. This volatile mix of apathy and aggression makes for a potent cocktail, one that the Capitol has carefully calibrated to maintain control. The character Plutarch Heavensbee is a direct nod to the esteemed Greek writer Plutarch, who rose through the ranks to become a prominent Roman citizen and one of the most respected sources for Classical historians. His extensive body of work includes approximately fifty surviving biographies of notable figures from ancient Greece and Rome, published under his influential Parallel Lives series. Despite often incorporating gossip and potentially unreliable information, Plutarch's writings offer invaluable insights into the mindset of 1st century Romans and have shaped public perceptions of these figures for centuries. His contributions to our understanding of this pivotal era in history are undeniable, making him a fitting inspiration for the character of Plutarch Heavensbee. Plutarch's experiences as both a Greek aristocrat and a prominent Roman citizen provide a unique perspective on the cultural and social dynamics at play during this time period. His writings often walked the fine line between fact and fiction, but their enduring influence is undeniable. As a historian and biographer, Plutarch was acutely aware of the power of storytelling to shape public opinion and influence perceptions of historical figures. His own works were carefully crafted to engage his audience and convey the complexities of ancient Greek and Roman society. The parallels between Plutarch's Rome and Panem are clear, particularly in the Capitol's use of entertainment and manipulation to maintain control over its citizens. The character of Plutarch Heavensbee serves as a reminder that even the most seemingly innocuous figures can have a profound impact on our understanding of history and its lessons. Suzanne Collins' father introduced her to the works of Plutarch at a young age, reading passages from his biographies that would later influence The Hunger Games series. Collins has mentioned that Plutarch Heavensbee was given his name because he embodies a sense of historical perspective, one of the few characters in the series who understands the broader context of the events unfolding around him. As a Capitol aristocrat, Heavensbee's education and upbringing would have exposed him to a sophisticated understanding of history, even if he had never known a world without the Hunger Games. His unique position as both a gamemaker and head of propaganda for the rebellion allowed him to shape public opinion and create compelling narratives that resonated with the masses. This is reminiscent of Plutarch's own role in shaping our understanding of ancient Greek and Roman history through his biographies, which continue to be studied today. The concept of the Hunger Games themselves draws on elements from both Greek mythology and Roman politics. One notable example can be found in the myth of Theseus. In this myth, the Cretan king was forced to send seven youths and maidens to Athens every year as a sacrifice to the Minotaur, only for an Athenian prince to volunteer to end the cycle by defeating the monster. The idea of each District providing a boy and girl as Tributes to the Capitol draws inspiration from both ancient Greece and Rome's political systems. This concept is rooted in the myth of Theseus, where a Cretan king forced Athens to send seven young men and women to Crete on a regular basis, only for them to be sent into a labyrinth to be killed by a minotaur. The mythological influence can also be seen in Katniss's character, who serves as a futuristic Theseus according to author Suzanne Collins. Katniss volunteers for certain death to protect innocents, echoing the bravery of the Athenian prince. But what about the word Tribute itself? Its origins lie in Latin, where Tributum referred to a form of taxation collected for military purposes. As Rome's empire expanded, however, citizens were exempt from paying this tax, and it instead became a price that conquered peoples paid as a sign of submission. In The Hunger Games, the Tributes serve as literal taxes paid by the districts after their defeat in the Dark Days, highlighting the brutal nature of the Capitol's rule. This concept is a far cry from the original purpose of taxation, which was meant to fund military campaigns and maintain order within the empire. When Katniss and Peeta arrive at the Capitol, they meet Effie, who warns them that Haymitch is their lifeline to the world - the difference between life and death. This concept of a mentor is ancient and has appeared in countless stories throughout history. However, there's an interesting connection between this idea and Greek mythology that might have influenced its use in The Hunger Games. In many stories, a mentor serves as a guide or advisor, often providing crucial support to the protagonist. Effie's warning also underscores the significance of Haymitch's role as Katniss and Peeta's Mentor, highlighting his importance in their survival within the arena. The concept of a mentor is not new, but its origins are deeply rooted in ancient Greek mythology. In Homer's epic poem The Odyssey, Mentor was a man who advised Telemachus during his father Odysseus' absence from Ithaca. Mentor's role went beyond mere guidance; he also served as an intermediary between the gods and mortals. Athena, disguised as Mentor, played a crucial part in ensuring Odysseus' safe return to Ithaca by advocating for him before the gods and providing his allies with vital information. The word mentor itself has its roots in Ancient Greek, meaning mind" or "thought". However, its usage as a name first appeared in The Odyssey. This raises questions about how The Hunger Games authors might have drawn inspiration from this ancient concept when creating Haymitch's role as Katniss and Peeta's mentor. Haymitch's actions in the arena are indeed pivotal to the survival of the two tributes, much like Athena's support for Odysseus. He provides them with crucial advice, advocates on their behalf to the sponsors, and guides them through the treacherous landscape of the Games. The parallels between Haymitch's role and Athena's in The Odyssey are striking. By drawing from this ancient mythology, the authors may have been intentionally creating a connection between Katniss and Peeta's experiences and those of Odysseus and Telemachus. Ultimately, the influence of Greek mythology on The Hunger Games is a testament to its enduring power to shape storytelling across cultures and centuries. articles.content: Dom Smales is launching a new creator management firm called WinnieWood Talent, which aims to help creators build lasting brands rather than focusing on short-term brand deals. WinnieWood will represent talent in the UK and Europe initially, with plans to expand to the US later on. The move marks a return for Smales to the industry after he sold his previous company, Gleam Futures, to advertising giant Dentsu in 2017. Smales founded Gleam Futures sixteen years ago, an innovative idea at the time that involved representing YouTubers like traditional talent. Among the notable creators who worked with Gleam was Zoella (Zoe Sugg), one of YouTube's earliest stars. The firm was eventually sold and its talent management arm formally closed in 2024, but Smales is now back with a new venture. WinnieWood will start by working with UK and European-based creators before expanding to the US market. WinnieWood is open to working with a wide range of creators across various social media platforms, including Substack. The company's focus is not solely on influencers with large follower counts but rather on identifying talented individuals who can drive engagement and generate revenue through their content. Unlike in the past when Smales was managing talent, the creator economy has undergone significant changes and has become increasingly sophisticated. This shift is reflected in the growing number of creators and the substantial investments being made in the market. WinnieWood's business model diverges from traditional talent management companies by offering a more comprehensive approach to supporting its creators' endeavors. In addition to securing brand deals, the firm will also provide financial backing through its investment arm. This injection of capital can aid creators in scaling their businesses and exploring new opportunities. The investment arm is expected to be a significant draw for creators looking to grow their enterprises. Smales notes that he often receives requests from companies seeking to include creators on their company's cap table, indicating a growing interest in partnering with content makers. By offering financial support, WinnieWood can help its clients navigate the complexities of business development. The firm's focus on building intellectual property (IP) with its creators sets it apart from other talent management companies. Rather than simply securing sponsorship deals, WinnieWood aims to collaborate with its clients on developing innovative projects, including shows, art, and other creative endeavors. This shift reflects a broader trend in which creators are increasingly taking ownership of their brands and pursuing new business ventures. articles.title: Portable Printing Revives Journaling Habit

articles.content: Journaling was a vital part of my teenage years, helping me cope with hormonal changes, school drama, and existential crises. It provided an outlet for my emotions and thoughts during a tumultuous period in life. However, when I left for college in another country, I abandoned this habit along with my cherished Nirvana cassettes. Despite making several attempts to revive journaling over the years, I never managed to stick to it consistently. I experimented with bullet journals to boost productivity but found it too time-consuming and gave up. Multiple notebooks and planners were also invested in, only to be left untouched eventually. The turning point came when I discovered the concept of portable printing on social media platforms. Journalers showcased vibrant pages adorned with photos from compact printers that fit seamlessly within their journals or planners. This idea resonated with me, and I became determined to incorporate it into my journaling practice. My decision to opt for a Polaroid Hi-Print pocket printer was influenced by my research into portable printing technology. I focused on finding a dye sublimation printer over the more common ZINK printers. Dye sublimation prints are renowned for their superior quality, achieved through layer-by-layer transfer of cyan, magenta, and yellow dyes followed by a protective coating. The benefits of using a dye sublimation printer became apparent as I began exploring my options. It offered higher image quality compared to ZINK printers, which rely on special paper that activates under heat without the need for ink. This distinction made it clear that dye sublimation was the better choice for someone seeking crisp and vibrant prints. The prospect of adding photos to my journal pages has reignited my passion for journaling. The process of printing small images using a portable printer excites me, allowing me to capture moments from everyday life and decorate my pages in a creative way. When I started looking for a portable printer to use with my journal, I knew I wanted photos on sticky paper to avoid any hassle when adding them to my pages. This led me to explore dye sublimation pocket printers, and one model that stood out was the Polaroid Hi-Print 2×3 Generation 2. The sleek design of this printer caught my eye immediately - its white color scheme, the prominent Polaroid logo, and a curved rainbow accent on the edge all contributed to its appeal. I must admit that I have a weakness for stylish products, which made it hard to resist purchasing the Hi-Print 2×3 "starter set". This bundle includes the printer itself along with two 2×3 paper cartridges. Each cartridge contains 10 photo sheets made of sticky back photo paper, exactly what I had been looking for. Both the newer Generation 2 and its predecessor, the original Generation 1 model, are widely available on the market. The main difference between these two versions lies in their charging ports: the Gen 2 uses a USB-C port, whereas the older one relies on Micro-USB. Getting started with the printer is relatively straightforward - after downloading the Polaroid Hi-Print app and pairing it with your phone, you're ready to print photos. The app's user interface is easy to navigate, allowing you to arrange multiple photos into collages rather than printing just a single image per sheet. You can also customize your prints by adding colorful frames or decorations through the app. The printer offers another feature that lets you create mosaics by combining multiple sheets to print one large image. The Hi-Print's printing process is a slow but deliberate one, as it uses dye sublimation to lay down colors in multiple passes. The first pass adds yellow, followed by magenta in the second, and subsequent passes add other hues until the final image is complete. This multi-pass approach results in a wait time of around 60 seconds per photo, which may seem like a drawback at first glance. However, the payoff is well worth it: the resulting photos are incredibly vibrant and sharp, with colors that pop off the page. One potential pitfall to consider is the cost of replacement cartridges, which can be pricey. A single pack of 20 sheets costs around $17, although purchasing in bulk can bring the price down slightly to approximately $14 per pack. Another limitation of the Hi-Print is its battery life, which may not be sufficient for frequent travelers or those who plan to use it on extended trips. With a 620mAh battery, Polaroid estimates that users will get up to 20 photo printing sessions before needing to recharge. Fortunately, recharging the Hi-Print doesn't take an eternity: according to Polaroid, it takes under an hour to top off the battery, which feels about right based on my own experience with the device. The compact size and portability of the Polaroid printer make it an ideal companion for capturing memories on the go. The thin photo sheets produced by the device are also a welcome feature, allowing journal entries to remain uncluttered and aesthetically pleasing. My experience with the printer has reignited my passion for creative expression through journaling. Even though I may not have access to all the nostalgia of my childhood, this portable printer has helped me recapture some of that lost joy in a modern way.
